steps.title: Load the quarter's filings
steps.prose: Reads the bundled CSV: one row per filing, carrying the client, the registrant, the reported spend and the filer's own free-text description of what they lobbied on. The data is synthetic — shaped like a Senate LDA export, describing no real filing.
steps.data_description: Every filing in the synthetic sample, exactly as the CSV records it.

steps.title: Keep the filings above $50,000
steps.prose: Drops every filing reporting less than $50,000 of spend for the period; exactly $50,000 is kept. The threshold is an editorial choice, not a fact about the data — check it is the line you would draw, because everything under it leaves here.
steps.data_description: The filings reporting at least $50,000; each drop is recorded, not silent.

steps.title: Read each filing's issue text
steps.prose: A model reads each surviving filing's `specific_issues` text and adds `policy_area`, `targets_specific_bill` and a one-sentence `primary_ask`. Check these against the issue text itself: the model's reading is the weakest link in the chain.
steps.data_description: The same filings, each carrying the model's three added judgments.

steps.title: Flag what needs a second look
steps.prose: Marks a filing for follow-up when it named no specific bill, or landed in the catch-all Other area — both mean the text did not pin down the ask. Plain code over the step above, so a wrong flag traces back to a wrong classification.
steps.data_description: Every surviving filing, plus the `needs_followup` flag.

steps.title: Publish the triage report
steps.prose: Writes the surviving filings out as one HTML page — client, registrant, spend, policy area and the follow-up flag. This is the artifact a reader sees, so every figure on it should be one you have followed back through the steps above.
steps.data_description: The published triage table: one row per surviving filing.
